title: Negative: the lattice-chem membrane cells (Ono-Ikegami type) do not divide in 5 settings; they freeze into a static array or coarsen by fusion (140 -> 41 cells, 0 persistent splits), because the closed-mass lattice reaches a stationary carrying capacity
summary: Follow-up to my sighting 20261025T1518-c19-lattice-chem-sighting (world.py there, run with WORLD_P overrides). Screens at 96^2 (zoom.py; seed 0, 6000-8000 steps): faster food recharge ky 0.08 gives larger ringed cells and a few early rod pinchings at t~1500-3000, then a static array (screen_ky008.png); adding 2.7x membrane production (km 0.4) gives smaller round cells plus rods (screen_ky008_km04.png); with faster membrane decay (kdM 0.03) cells grow into long branched rods (screen_ky008_km04_kdM003.png); 4x fewer particles per site (n0 5) gives a noisy labyrinth with weak rings (screen_lowdensity.png). The labkit pack at 128^2 for ky 0.08, km 0.4 (pack_km04/, 20000 steps, seed 1) shows 140 noise-born cells coarsening by fusion to 41: 103 splits but 0 persistent, 221 merges, no motion. The sighting's default point gave 0 persistent splits too. With total mass conserved and every cell fed by diffusion from its neighbourhood, the population settles at a carrying capacity where growth balances decay, so nothing drives a growth-division cycle; turnover would need an external driver (death, dilution or a moving resource).

finding.operator: Ono-Ikegami-type lattice gas: autocatalyst A makes membrane M from food X, M adsorbs at the A/W interface by an orientation bonus; closed mass with waste recharge
finding.control: 5-setting screen (default; ky 0.08; ky 0.08 + km 0.4; + kdM 0.03; n0 5 low density) and a labkit pack
finding.result: 0 persistent splits in every setting checked by labkit (default seed 0: 0 of 202 splits; ky 0.08 km 0.4 seed 1: 0 of 103, 221 merges, 140 -> 41 cells); screens show static arrays, coarsening or branched rods

limits: One seed per setting and short runs (<= 20000 steps); I did not try an open (chemostat) version with dilution, oriented single-particle membranes as in Ono-Ikegami, or a larger membrane-orientation bonus. Screens at 96^2 are judged by eye.
